units.text: My name is Mitch.
I want to tell you about the thing that visited me after I moved into my brother's house.
I used to call ghosts nonsense.
Then something climbed through my window with empty black eyes, and I stopped laughing at nonsense.
Let us go back to the beginning.
A week after my own house was foreclosed, I moved in with my brother Edwin.
We had not spoken in ten years, so I was glad to be there, and that first night I fell asleep fast, happy for once.
Around one in the morning I heard rustling outside my window.
I told myself it was only a raccoon and went back to sleep.
In the morning I mentioned it to Edwin, and he agreed it was probably nothing.
The next night I woke to the sound of my window sliding open, then a heavy thump on the floor, as if something had climbed inside.
I sat up and searched the room, but I saw nothing there.
"You look terrible this morning, Mitch."
Edwin dropped his coffee cup the moment he saw my face.
He held up a mirror for me.
A long gash had opened across my left cheek overnight, and I had no memory of how it got there.
At the hospital the doctor lifted my shirt to show me a fresh, sewn incision where a kidney should have been.
"You somehow lost your left kidney last night. We do not know how. I am sorry, Mitch."
I could not answer him.
On the third night I woke at midnight to a creature leaning over my bed, a dark hoodie pulled low, a cracked blue mask with no mouth and no nose.
Where its eyes should have been there was only black, empty sockets, with a black fluid dripping from them.
It lunged for my chest with long pale fingers, clawing for my ribs.
I grabbed the camera from the mantel and took one picture before I kicked it hard in the face and ran.
I grabbed my wallet and fled into the dark woods behind the house, until I tripped on a rock and everything went black.
I woke again in a hospital bed with only minor injuries.
The doctor said my parents were coming to collect me, and then his face changed.
"Your brother has been killed by some... thing. I am sorry."
My parents drove me back to gather my remaining things.
In the hallway lay Edwin's body, and beside it something small.
I picked it up without telling my parents what I had found, and in the car I finally looked down at what I was holding.
This story is inspired by the Eyeless Jack creepypasta, first written and shared online in twenty twelve.
Now tell me.
Would you have believed it was only a raccoon?
